REQ-A0.evidence: 400 random graphs compared with brute-force simple-path enumeration; zero-cost cycle paths are simple
REQ-A0.superseded: A0's default equal-cost tie order (fewest edges, then lexical) is replaced by REQ-A3. It is still available as Graph(tie_policy='fewest_hops'), which is what the A0 tie tests use.

REQ-A1.implementation: routing_graph.py: shortest(src, dst, *, blocked=(), max_hops=None); the hop bound is applied during the search
REQ-A1.tests: test_routing_graph.py: BlockedAndHopBound (cheap 4-hop cost-4 route vs max_hops=1 giving cost-10 s->t), FinalTiePolicy random trials
REQ-A1.evidence: 300 random trials (fewest_hops) plus 250 random trials for each tie policy, checked against bounded brute force

REQ-A2.implementation: routing_graph.py: Graph.snapshot() -> GraphSnapshot (read-only, mapping proxies, frozen version and tie_policy); Graph.apply(changes, *, expected_version=None)
REQ-A2.evidence: snapshot is unchanged after the graph changes; 9 invalid batches roll back; ConflictError is raised before an invalid batch is applied; no-change batches leave version alone

REQ-A3.implementation: routing_graph.py: Graph(tie_policy='lexical'|'fewest_hops'), default 'lexical'; lexical search keeps distinct simple prefixes so the visited-set and hop-bound alternatives survive
REQ-A3.evidence: the longer, lexically smaller zero-cost route s,a,b,t wins by default; fewest_hops gives s,t; snapshots keep their policy; a bounded case needing a hop-limited prefix is tested; random trials run for both policies

REQ-B0.implementation: booking_calendar.py: Calendar(capacity), reserve, cancel, available, allocations, CapacityError, ConflictError
REQ-B0.evidence: 100-way overlap; staircase; 60x120 random operations checked against a naive per-instant model

REQ-B1.implementation: booking_calendar.py: reserve_many(requests), replace(id, start, end, units=1)
REQ-B1.evidence: duplicate inside a batch, cumulative overload within a batch, and invalid shapes all leave state unchanged; replace excludes its own old booking; a failed replace keeps the original

REQ-B2.implementation: booking_calendar.py: wait, waiting, promote; cancel also covers waiting ids; reserve/reserve_many/replace cannot take waiting ids
REQ-B2.evidence: order is higher priority first, then FIFO; promote skips and continues ([p1,p3,p4]); earlier promotions block later ones; no auto-promotion

REQ-B3.implementation: booking_calendar.py: checkpoint() -> CalendarCheckpoint (immutable, owner token), restore(cp), read-only version
REQ-B3.evidence: restore keeps the exact FIFO (w3,w1,w2) and new waits queue behind it; checkpoints are reusable; foreign or invalid checkpoints raise ValueError; version goes 0..11 with no-ops unchanged and forward-only restore

REQ-C0.tests: test_inventory_stream.py: Parsing, Validation, Idempotency, FailureContinuation, RandomizedModel
REQ-C0.evidence: 300 random fragment splits (inside quotes and between CR and LF), char-by-char feeding, 80 random streams checked against a model

REQ-C1.implementation: inventory_stream.py: kind 'batch' with ops applied in order on staged balances, all-or-nothing, nested batches and id-bearing ops rejected
REQ-C1.evidence: later ops consume earlier stock; 6 invalid batches roll back without reserving the id and are then retried successfully; empty batch is recorded

REQ-C2.implementation: inventory_stream.py: undo(event_id) using the net signed per-SKU delta; tombstone kept
REQ-C2.evidence: a net-delta case where replaying ops in reverse order would fail; a negative undo fails unchanged and can be retried; a repeated tombstoned line is ignored and changed content raises ConflictError

REQ-C3.implementation: inventory_stream.py: checkpoint() -> InventoryCheckpoint, restore(cp); MAX_LINE = 4096 code points checked before any line is applied
REQ-C3.evidence: an unfinished fragment completes after restore; idempotency and undo state are as of the checkpoint; 4096 accepted vs 4097 rejected with multi-byte characters; an overlong feed rolls back its earlier complete events and its buffer

A: add_node returns bool; set_edge returns None; remove_edge with an unknown endpoint raises ValueError
Self-loop edges are allowed but never used, since paths must be simple
apply change dicts use the 'op' key ('kind'/'type' are accepted aliases); extra keys are invalid; apply returns the new version; version advances only if the final state differs
blocked must be a non-str iterable of known node names
B: units above capacity give CapacityError, not ValueError
Waiting ids are not replaceable (replace on one raises ValueError)
replace with identical values is a no-op and does not bump version
C: Unknown or extra JSON keys, duplicate keys and NaN/Infinity are invalid
On a semantic failure, feed raises at once; the failing line is consumed; earlier ids from that call are on exc.applied; later complete lines stay buffered for the next feed/finish
Line length excludes the LF/CRLF terminator; a trailing CR in an unfinished buffer is treated as a possible terminator
